RoomType.rationale: MechaKnightElite.cs:10 `RoomType => RoomType.Elite`. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass (monsters/base.py) carries no `RoomType` field at all -- the type is modeled structurally by which of `ActRooms`'s four key tuples (`weak_keys`/`normal_keys`/`elite_keys`/`boss_keys`) an encounter id is listed under (rooms.py:67-70, field decls). `mecha_knight` is in `elite_keys`, matching `RoomType.Elite`, and this also drives the gold ladder (see the guard below) and the `EliteEncounter` room-visit accessor (`RoomSet.next_elite_encounter`, rooms.py:549). Same observable, different architecture -- one shared mechanism across all nine of this batch's units; see `encounter/_room_type_and_weak` in the report.

AllPossibleMonsters.issue: MechaKnightElite.cs:12 returns a single-element list containing `MechaKnight` (ModelDb.Monster<MechaKnight>()). The sim has no `AllPossibleMonsters` analogue anywhere (`grep -rn AllPossibleMonsters sts2_rl/` returns nothing) -- confirmed shared across all nine units in this batch, filed once under `encounter/_all_possible_monsters`. Cost, enumerated from the game side (`grep -rn AllPossibleMonsters src/Core` and then grepping every consumer of `ActModel.AllMonsters`/`ModelDb.Monsters`): exactly THREE consumers game-wide, all debug/UI -- `UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68` and `:147` (dev-console `monsters`/`unlock` commands) and `NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164` (the stats-screen "monsters killed / total" achievement ratio). None affect RNG, roster generation, combat, or rewards. Dormant: the headless sim has no dev console and no stats screen, so nothing in it could read the value even if it existed.

GetCameraScaling.rationale: Presentation only (camera framing for the combat scene). MechaKnightElite.cs:14-17 returns 0.9f / Vector2.Down*50f; the headless sim has no camera or scene rendering at all.

GetCameraOffset.rationale: Presentation only, same as GetCameraScaling above.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ROSTER: MechaKnightElite.cs:24-27 returns exactly one `(MechaKnight, null)` pair; `MECHA_KNIGHT_ELITE = Encounter(id="mecha_knight_elite", monster_classes=[MechaKnight])` (mecha_knight.py:81-84) -- one monster, same class, matching count and identity. ORDER: trivially matches (single element). SLOT: C# passes `null` (no override of `Slots`, no slot argument construction); the sim's `Encounter.monster_slots` defaults to `()` so `seat_in_slots`'s `zip(monsters, self.monster_slots)` (base.py:472, called from `create_monsters`) assigns nothing, leaving `slot_name` at its default `None` -- both sides null. DRAW COUNT: zero on both sides. `MechaKnightElite.GenerateMonsters` (MechaKnightElite.cs:24-27) never touches `base.Rng` -- confirmed by reading the whole file, no `Rng.NextItem`/`NextInt` call anywhere in it. `Encounter.create_monsters` explicitly does not draw for a fixed composition: `monsters/base.py:477-478`'s own comment states "Fixed composition draws no RNG, so the parity selection_rng (when present) is simply unused here." 0 == 0.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by MechaKnightElite. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass (monsters/base.py:353-479) is never passed to `HookSystem.register` anywhere in the codebase (`grep -rn 'hooks.register' sts2_rl/` finds Monster/Card/Relic/Potion/Affliction/Enchantment instances registering themselves, never an `Encounter`) -- the encounter object is never a hook listener on either side, so the `false` is honoured by construction rather than by an explicit flag.

guards.what: Draw count / stream independence of the per-encounter Rng (EncounterModel.Rng)
guards.rationale: Stream IDENTITY (which seed, which formula) is `seam/rng_streams`'s subject, not this record's -- but the DRAW COUNT is mine per the task brief, and it is zero: MechaKnightElite.GenerateMonsters never calls `base.Rng` (see the GenerateMonsters hook above), so the per-encounter Rng's independence guarantee (EncounterModel.cs:41-48's doc comment: "safe to do... because we don't need to keep track of a given encounter's RNG state once it's over") is never even exercised by this unit -- there is nothing to desynchronise. `make_encounter_rng` (sts2_rl/rng.py:52-67) exists and reproduces the seed formula bit-for-bit for encounters that DO draw; this unit is not one of them.

guards.what: The Niche HP-roll mechanism, checked specifically as the lead this batch's brief names for `enemy id 151 vs 148` / the 933T Mecha Knight divergence
guards.rationale: Investigated and RULED OUT as an encounter-tier explanation. MechaKnight.MinInitialHp == MaxInitialHp == 300 (both non-ascension; per monster/mecha_knight.json, already audited faithful). `Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue` (Creature.cs:371-383) still draws exactly ONE value off `RunState.Rng.Niche` even when min==max (`hashSet = {300}`, `hashSet.Count<=0` is false, so `rng.NextItem(hashSet)` fires -- one `NextInt` call). The sim's `CombatState._roll_parity_hp`/`_assign_parity_monster_hp` (combat.py:423-456) reproduces this exactly: `candidates=[300]` (nothing else on the enemy side has HP 300 to exclude, since Mecha Knight is the encounter's only monster), so `niche.next_int_range(0, 1)` fires -- one draw, same as the game, for the same degenerate reason. This is also independently corroborated by `audit/records/seam/rng_streams.json`'s `RunRngType.Niche` row, already verdicted `faithful for the HP-roll path (wired directly via CombatState._niche, not through CombatRng)` -- not re-verdicted here per rule 3, only confirmed by execution. CONCLUSION: neither this encounter's GenerateMonsters (0 draws, matches) nor the Niche HP-roll (1 draw, matches, and the roll is a no-variance degenerate pick on both sides) can produce an off-by-N draw-count desync at this unit. The `+3-HP cascade` the task brief also names was already explained and fixed by a DIFFERENT, unrelated mechanism -- the Unsettling Lamp / Artifact `PowerCmd.apply` ordering bug (memory note `unsettling-lamp-artifact-order`; Dominate's Strength-from-Vulnerable calc, (23+10)*1.5=49 vs (23+8)*1.5=46 -- nothing to do with the encounter's roster or draw stream). The `enemy id 151 vs 148` figure itself could not be located in any test, doc, or memory file in this repo (searched `audit/`, `docs/`, `.superpowers/`, `test/` and the memory index) -- if it is a real observation from a since-superseded session, its cause is not a draw-count or slot-order defect in ANY of this batch's nine `GenerateMonsters` implementations, all nine of which draw zero and all nine of which this record's siblings independently confirm. Not ruled out: a creature-COUNT (not draw-count) desync from an EARLIER encounter in the run creating a different number of enemies than the game before Mecha Knight is reached, which would shift the cumulative Niche counter without any single roll being individually wrong -- `encounter/axebots`' and `encounter/knights'` slot-order dormant findings in this same batch are the closest candidates, but both are independently proven unobservable (see their own records) and neither changes a CREATURE COUNT, only a creature's `slot_name`, so neither is a counter-shifting mechanism either. No live gap found; nothing in this batch's nine units explains the delta.
